title: Final: anatomy of a model
sub: Vertices, normals, UVs and the scene: test yourself
cards/0/task: Build the house with every triangle facing you.
cards/1/q: How many triangles do you get from one quad?
cards/1/explain: A quad is cut along a diagonal into two triangles.
cards/2/q: Which OBJ line sets a UV coordinate?
cards/2/explain: vt is a texture vertex, that is, a UV. vn is a normal, f is a face.
cards/3/q: A triangle is listed clockwise as you look at it. What do you see with backface culling on?
cards/3/options/0: Nothing: its back is facing you
cards/3/explain: Counterclockwise winding counts as the front.
cards/4/q: A cube with sharp edges: how many vertices does the GPU need?
cards/4/explain: Three copies of each corner, one for each face with its own normal.
cards/5/task: Make the mug in glTF stand upright and be 10 cm tall.
cards/6/q: What do OBJ and STL not store? Select all.
cards/6/explain: Every mesh has vertices. But these old formats have no units, hierarchy or animation.
cards/7/q: A model arrived gray. What do you check first?
cards/7/options/0: Whether the material and texture files were included
cards/7/explain: External textures are the thing most often lost in transit.
cards/8/pairs/3/1: The back side is not drawn
